scope: Proposition 9.1 (Uniform contraction on a fixed block) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 97. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < ξ < λ, a polynomial envelope M, a horizon constant A < ∞, and H < ∞. There are deterministic constants D, b0 < ∞ and disorder events of probability tending to one on which the following assertion holds simultaneously for all starting configurations, all such terminal functions, and all b0 ≤ a < a + D ≤ T ≤ A log n: N2 a ≤ e−2(λ−ξ)D N2 a+D + n−H . (9.3) The same assertion, with no burn-in, holds in the deterministic typicality convention of Theorem 5.1 for families of initial laws satisfying log ∥ dν/ dµ∥∞ = o(n) uniformly. The constants may be chosen after H and M; no quantitative rate for a fixed-time o(1) is asserted or required.
